samples.text:
Today, celebrities such as singers, actors and sports players are very popular, especially among young people. Some people think famous people must be role models, while others believe they should be free to live how they want. I will discuss both views and give my own opinion.

On one hand, many people believe that celebrities have a responsibility to behave well. Young people follow them on social media every day and often copy their clothes, their language and their behaviour. If a famous footballer takes drugs or a singer drink too much alcohol, teenagers may think that it is cool to do the same. Also, celebrities earn a lot of money because of their fans, so they should give something back by being a good example.

On the other hand, some people argue that celebrities are normal human who make mistakes like everyone else. They did not choose to be role models, they only wanted to be a good actor or athlete. It is not fair that their private life is always in the newspapers. Furthermore, parents and teachers should be the main role models for children, not people on the television.

In my opinion, celebrities should try to behave responsibly in public, because they have big influence on young people. However, they also deserve some privacy in their personal life. The media should not report every small mistake they make.

In conclusion, both views have some points. I believe that famous people have some responsibility to be a good role model, but they should also have freedom in their private life, and parents should teach children not to copy celebrities blindly.

samples.text:
In an age of social media, celebrities have more influence over young people than ever before. Some believe that this influence brings a responsibility to act as a positive role model, while others argue that famous people should be free to live as they choose. In my opinion, celebrities do have some responsibility, but it should be limited to their public behaviour.

Those who expect celebrities to set a good example point to the powerful effect they have on young fans. Teenagers frequently imitate the appearance, attitudes and lifestyles of the stars they admire, and a famous person who glamorises reckless behaviour, such as dangerous driving or excessive drinking, may encourage others to copy them. Moreover, celebrities benefit enormously from public attention, earning fame and wealth through the support of their fans. It therefore seems reasonable that they should accept certain obligations in return.

On the other hand, many argue that it is unfair to impose such expectations. Most celebrities became famous because of a particular talent, such as acting, singing or playing sport, not because they wanted to guide young people's moral development. They are ordinary human beings who inevitably make mistakes, and constant media scrutiny of their private lives can cause them considerable stress. Critics of the role-model idea also suggest that responsibility for young people's values lie primarily with parents, teachers and communities.

I believe a balanced position is most appropriate. Celebrities should be aware of their influence and avoid promoting harmful behaviour in their public statements, performances and social media posts. However, their private lives should be respected, and it is unrealistic to expect them to be perfect.

In conclusion, although celebrities should not be forced to act as moral guides in every aspect of their lives, I believe they have a responsibility to use their public platform in a way that does not harm the young people who admire them.
samples.why: Clear position throughout · both views extended with relevant examples · logical paragraphing and varied cohesion · good collocations (media scrutiny, glamorises reckless behaviour) · mostly error-free with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
The influence of celebrities on young people has grown enormously with the rise of social media, prompting debate about what, if anything, famous people owe their audiences. Some argue that celebrity brings with it a duty to act as a role model, whereas others contend that public figures are entitled to live as they please. In my view, celebrities have a genuine but limited responsibility, one that applies to their public conduct rather than to every aspect of their lives.

Those who believe celebrities should be role models emphasise the scale of their influence. Young people often identify closely with the stars they follow, adopting their styles, opinions and habits, and when a well-known figure normalises behaviour such as heavy drinking or casual cruelty online, the effects can ripple through a large and impressionable audience. Furthermore, celebrities derive their wealth and status from public admiration, so it seems fair to expect them to recognise the obligations that accompany such privilege.

On the other hand, there are strong grounds for resisting this expectation. Fame is frequently a by-product of talent in a particular field, and a gifted athlete or musician has not necessarily chosen, or trained, to serve as a moral example. Demanding flawless conduct from them is not only unrealistic but can also justify intrusive media coverage of their private lives. Moreover, placing the burden of guiding young people on celebrities risks diverting attention from those who should bear it primarily, namely parents, educators and communities.

Balancing these arguments, I believe celebrities should be expected to exercise care in how they use their public platforms, avoiding the promotion of harmful behaviour, while their private lives should largely remain their own. At the same time, young people should be taught to admire achievement without uncritically imitating the individuals behind it.

In conclusion, although celebrities cannot reasonably be required to be perfect, their considerable influence carries a responsibility to act with care in public, even as they retain the right to a private life.
samples.why: Both views fully developed and balanced · clear, carefully qualified position · skilful cohesion and logical sequencing · wide, precise vocabulary (impressionable, by-product, intrusive) · wide range of accurate complex structures.
